Define a Pydantic model for an item, then give your order model an attribute typed as a list of that item model. You can also use Pydantic models as subtypes of `list`, `set`, etc.[3], and you can define arbitrarily deeply nested models[4].

The docs show this with an `Offer` that holds a list of `Item`s. You can use the same pattern for an order:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    price: float
    tax: float | None = None


class Offer(BaseModel):   # e.g. rename to Order
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    price: float
    items: list[Item]


@app.post("/offers/")
async def create_offer(offer: Offer):
    return offer
```

The parameter is read from the body because function parameters that are declared to be Pydantic models should be **taken from the request body**[2]. The client then sends JSON with an `items` array of item objects.

If the body should be just the list, with no wrapping order object, you can declare the type in the parameter of the function, the same as in Pydantic models[4], for example `items: list[Item]`.
